How transit in the Tahoe Region is paid for, route by route

This model brings the region's transit operating costs and funding sources into one place, with the goal of providing transparency and showing the trade-offs of future funding options.

This tool is a draft undergoing further review and stakeholder validation.

Today

Existing funding conditions

A snapshot of how all transit operating revenue sources are currently budgeted in fiscal year (FY) 26-27.

Inputs users can change

Inputs, assumptions, and rules

These pages allow users to edit service hours, operating cost rates, funding amounts, model assumptions, and how each funding source is split across routes. Use the Reset button in the top right corner to reset to original inputs.

Results and future

One-year and five-year outlooks

The One-year outlook shows the balance for a selected fiscal year by route, agency, and jurisdiction. The Five-year outlook projects each agency's balance through FY 30-31. The Agreements and risk page lists funding agreements and time-limited funds. All three pages update as users change inputs and assumptions.

How to use this page

Your edits update the outlook pages right away. They save in your browser only, and don't impact the model for other users.

  • How to edit: Blue cells are inputs. Click one, type a new value, and press Enter. A red bar on the left edge of a cell marks a value you changed.
  • Editable values:
    • Funding sources: Type a new FY 26-27 amount in the blue cell. Select Details next to a source to change its amount, match requirement, restrictions, projection, and commitment. Sources in the same program are grouped. Select a program name to show its lines.
    • Services: In Services and operating costs, change a service's agency, operator, trips, hours, miles, or cost per hour.
    • New services: In Service plan elements, check Include on a service from the Tahoe Transit Study plan. To model a service that is not in the plan, open Add a new service and enter its operator, start year, and annual cost or service hours.
    • Jurisdiction miles: In Jurisdiction miles by service, type the annual miles each service runs in each jurisdiction. Your numbers replace the even-split placeholders.
    • Route shares: How each source splits across routes is on the Allocation and rules page.
  • Want to start over? Select Reset at the top of the page to return the whole scenario to the source data.
  • Submit a change to the inputs: If your agency's numbers differ from what is shown, select Submit as a data update at the top of the page. TRPA will review each request and update the model for everyone.

Model assumptions

Opening balance carried into FY 26-27

Enter each agency's FY 25-26 ending operating reserve if known. Leave at $0 to start from the FY 26-27 budget alone.

Services and operating costs

Annual cost is vehicle service hours (VSH) times the operator's cost per hour, unless a cost is entered directly. Urban and rural classes drive FTA 5307 and 5311 eligibility. Service type drives ADA rules.

InputChanged from source

Source: operator service data and FY 26-27 cost estimates compiled for the Tahoe Transit Study3, and route conditions from the study's scenario analysis2. The Main Line counts as its three segments, with cost split by service hours.

Private and non-federalized operators. Add ski, resort, or airport shuttles with "Federalized" unchecked to see them in the regional picture. The model blocks federal funds from them.

Operator cost rates

Fully allocated operating cost per vehicle service hour and the annual escalator used for the five-year outlook.

Source: operator cost per hour compiled for the Tahoe Transit Study3.

Jurisdiction miles by service

Annual service miles each service runs in each jurisdiction. The split sets the California and Nevada portions used by state-restricted sources, caps jurisdiction-restricted sources, and drives the jurisdiction results. Until miles by jurisdiction are available, each service's total service miles are split evenly as a placeholder. Services with no service miles in the data show no placeholder miles. Enter miles for each jurisdiction to set their split.

Placeholders split each service equally among the jurisdictions it serves2. Lake Link zones follow TRPA direction (Nov. 20, 2026): Zone 1 is 75 percent City of South Lake Tahoe and 25 percent Douglas County, Zone 2 is Douglas County, and Zone 3 is City of South Lake Tahoe. SSTMA's cost-share method averages shares of miles, hours, stops, and ridership4.

Service plan elements

Recommended changes from the Tahoe Transit Study service plan, with their annual marginal cost, and any new services you add below. Check "Include" to add one to the scenario. It then appears as a service users can fund on Allocation and rules.

TART 30-minute peak: how the cost splits across routes

The TART 30-minute peak row adds its cost to these routes. The TART 2025 Systems Plan gives a systemwide total of $2,683,400 and 16,100 added service hours a year. The model splits both by each route's annual service hours. The split is a placeholder until TART provides a route breakdown. Editing a route's service hours under Services and costs changes its share.

TART 2025 Systems Plan Update.

Add a new service

Model a service that is not in the plan. Enter either its annual cost in the year it starts, or its annual service hours. Hours are priced at the operator's cost per hour. Either way, the cost grows each year after by the operator's escalator. To fund a new service, choose its start year or later in the Fiscal year menu, then set its shares on Allocation and rules.

Revenue projections by source

Type a value into any future year to override the rule for that year. Clear the cell to return to the rule.

InputChanged from source

Source: Tahoe Transit Study financial plan1. FTA growth 1 percent per year. TDA follows RTP projected population change (0.025 percent per year).

FTA 5307 sub-allocation between TTD and Placer County

The Lake Tahoe urbanized area (UZA) apportionment is split by an earned-share formula: the average of each operator's share of urban revenue miles, population, and ridership. 75 percent of 5307 goes to operations. The method is documented in the FTA sub-allocation MOU between the agencies.

Source: Tahoe Transit Study FTA split3. FY 26-27 values are the FY 25-26 apportionment plus 1 percent, an estimate.

How to read this page

This page shows one fiscal year in detail. Pick the year in the Fiscal year menu above the results. It updates as soon as you change an input.

  • By route: Each service's operating cost and the funding applied to it. A gap means its funding does not cover its cost.
  • By agency: Each agency's revenue, the cost of the services it runs, and its ending balance.
  • By jurisdiction: The cost each jurisdiction's share of service leaves for local funds, compared with the local funding it pays.
  • Flags and notes: The count at the top of the page. Select it to see each rule the funding breaks.
  • Change the results: Edit funding amounts, services, and costs on Inputs and assumptions, or route shares on Allocation and rules. Your changes are listed below.

How to read this page

This page projects each agency's revenue, operating cost, and ending balance from FY 26-27 to FY 30-31. It updates as soon as you change an input.

  • Revenue and cost: Bars are revenue each year by funding level. The dashed line is operating cost in the source data. The solid line is operating cost with your changes, including any services you add.
  • Ending balance by agency: Each agency's revenue minus the cost of the services it runs. Bars below zero are deficits. The table under each chart shows the numbers.
  • Funding cliffs: Sources that end within the five years are listed at the bottom of the page.
  • Change the results: On Inputs and assumptions, you can:
    • Add planned services, or the TART 30-minute peak, in Service plan elements, or model a service that is not in the plan.
    • Change funding amounts in Funding sources, or future years in Revenue projections.
    • Change cost per hour or the yearly escalator in Operator cost rates.
    • Carry surpluses forward, count federal funds above the cap, or set opening balances in Model assumptions.

        It is a starting point based on the model's rules. It is not an optimized or recommended funding plan. It assigns funds in this order:

        1. Earmarked sources and fares go to the services they are tied to.
        2. Federal funds go next, up to each route's federal share cap.
        3. Flexible funds cover each route's remaining cost, most restricted source first.

        Funds stay with the agency that receives them. Each source's own rules apply: its restrictions by state, jurisdiction, route, service type, and urban or rural area, and its federal share cap. After it runs, review the rule checks and adjust shares by hand where needed.

        To undo it, select Reset at the top of the page. Reset returns the whole scenario to the source data. It also removes any other edits you made. Export to Excel first to keep a record of them.
